TAKEAWAYS
Total Revenue
-- EUR 247 million, including EUR 197 million from YORVIPATH, EUR 44 million from SKYTROFA, and EUR 6 million in collaboration revenue.
YORVIPATH Revenue Adjustment
-- Revenue was reduced by approximately EUR 15 million due to a temporary U.S. free drug program and a onetime event affecting Europe Direct, as detailed by management.
YORVIPATH U.S. Patient Growth
-- Over 1,000 new patients prescribed the drug in the quarter, bringing cumulative U.S. prescriptions to more than 6,300 across over 2,700 unique health care providers.
SKYTROFA U.S. Market Share
-- Product held a 7% share of the overall growth hormone market, with ongoing steady demand in both pediatric and adult segments.
YUVIWEL U.S. Launch
-- More than 60 children were prescribed YUVIWEL within the first 4-5 weeks post-launch, involving over 35 unique prescribers, with reimbursement approvals reported "as fast as a few days."
Operating Profit
-- IFRS operating profit reached EUR 25 million (10% margin); non-IFRS operating profit was EUR 55 million (22% margin).
Non-IFRS Net Profit
-- EUR 18 million, or EUR 0.27 per share; reported net profit of EUR 629 million included a EUR 679 million deferred tax asset.
Cash Position
-- EUR 573 million in cash and cash equivalents at period end, reflecting EUR 60 million spent on share repurchase and settlement of RSUs.
Product Pipeline Activity
-- Over 20 ongoing or planned clinical trials for label and market expansion, including 4 new clinical entities in preclinical development.
Combination Therapy Data
-- COACH Phase II trial for hypochondroplasia showed a threefold efficacy improvement on height score over monotherapy at 52 weeks and enhancements in lower limb alignment and arm strength.
TransCon IL-2 Oncology Strategy
-- Median overall survival improved to 10 months in late-stage ovarian cancer, but internal oncology development was discontinued to pursue other strategic options for the asset.
PRV Sale
-- Agreement to sell a Priority Review Voucher for USD 187.5 million in cash, awarded upon YUVIWEL U.S. approval.
Direct Listing and Debt Redemption
-- Transition to direct NASDAQ listing completed in April, followed by full redemption of outstanding convertible senior notes in May.
Insurance Coverage for YORVIPATH
-- Upstream coverage now includes approximately 80% of U.S. patient lives, with cumulative approval rate reported near the mid-70% range.
Clinical Expansion
-- Ongoing U.S. trials for YORVIPATH dose escalation from 30 to 60 micrograms and geographic label expansion for YUVIWEL highlighted by management.
SUMMARY
The quarter marked an operational turning point with the FDA approval of YUVIWEL, resulting in three products now approved across four distinct rare endocrine indications. Management reported EUR 247 million in revenue, driven largely by YORVIPATH and SKYTROFA, despite EUR 15 million in adverse adjustments from reimbursement and market access transitions. The company disclosed rapid patient adoption of YORVIPATH and early demand for YUVIWEL, suggesting sustained momentum. Pipeline progress included combination therapy data in hypochondroplasia, the discontinuation of internal TransCon IL-2 oncology work, continued partnership initiatives, and a significant USD 187.5 million cash inflow from the PRV sale. Net profit reflected a one-off deferred tax asset while underlying non-IFRS profit and cash positions indicated improved operational performance.
Management described Q1 as a pivotal moment, citing "rapid revenue growth," achieved profitability, and expansion in both commercialization and R&D.
Jan Mikkelsen stated, "March was our last revenue month ever for YORVIPATH, supported by an increased number of new patients, as well as patients returning to reimbursement from free drug."
New patient enrollments and prescriber adoption showed quarter-over-quarter growth, confirmed by Jay Wu’s note of "about 300-plus" additional prescribers.
CEO Jan Mikkelsen asserted that the insurance approval trends and "foundation for revenue growth" remain "consistent with our guidance," reinforcing outlook continuity.
Jay Wu clarified, "over half approved within 8 weeks of enrollment," referencing improvements in reimbursement speed for YORVIPATH.
R&D expense fell to EUR 59 million, benefiting from an EUR 11 million inventory write-up following YUVIWEL FDA approval and reduced clinical activity.
SG&A expense rose to EUR 145 million, attributed to global commercial expansion.
Net finance expense, predominantly non-cash, was EUR 63 million, including a EUR 34 million remeasurement loss on liabilities; net cash financial expense was EUR 1 million.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
TransCon
: A proprietary technology platform used by Ascendis Pharma to develop long-acting versions of therapeutic molecules.
Priority Review Voucher (PRV)
: A transferrable U.S. FDA-issued certificate granting expedited review for a future drug application.
COACH trial
: Phase II clinical trial evaluating combination therapy with TransCon CNP and TransCon Growth Hormone for hypochondroplasia.
EU Europe Direct
: Ascendis’s direct commercialization strategy in certain European countries, as referenced by management regarding one-time revenue impacts.
